fieldMarks: Back scales fairly large, keeled and pointed (prickly look); gray, brown or black with wavy dark and light bands or V-shaped blotches, often 5-10 dark rows.
Rear of the thighs yellow or orange; solid blue belly patches and throat in males, faint or absent in females and young.
Breeding males may have blue or greenish dorsal scales and enlarged postanal scales; never a blue tail.
Up to about 9.5-9.9 cm snout-vent length.
behavior: Usually on the ground or low perches (logs, fences) but sometimes climbs bushes or trees; moves to the far side of a trunk when approached.
Adult males defend home ranges during the breeding season; seasonal home range under 0.01 ha in central California.
Eats mainly insects and spiders; eggs buried in loose soil, clutch 3-17, hatching mostly August-September.
Inactive in cold weather; emerges in late winter or early spring.
habitat: Grassland, sagebrush, woodland, open conifer forest, rocky canyons, talus slopes and fence rows.
Not in severe desert but reaches mountain slopes near it.
range: Washington and southeastern Idaho south through Oregon, California, Nevada and western Utah to northwestern Baja California; sea level to about 3,350 m. Non-native in Montana.

lookalikes.name: Common sagebrush lizard
lookalikes.howToTell: Smaller scales with shorter spines and pale dorsolateral stripes; no yellow on the thighs.

lookalikes.name: Western skink
lookalikes.howToTell: Smooth, shiny scales and a blue tail in young.
